sessions.title: MoonBoard benchmarks
sessions.details: Red Curry, Harvey Climbs Hard, Squiggly Boulder, Another Day, Blue Nun (5 problems, 5 completed, 7 tries)

plan.what: 20mm half-crimp hangs at a percentage of your Tindeq peak, set each week by the cycle (see Cycle). Left hand first, then one-arm progressions as the weeks get heavier.
plan.spacing: At least 2 days from Board; same day as Pull

plan.what: Tension benchmark lists or MoonBoard benchmarks (both at 40°), alternating.
One main pull (weighted pullups, one-arm slow declines or lock offs), then rotator cuff rows and I Y T shoulder raises.

Gym strengthening for your weak spots: pinch block lifts, heel hook floor raises, ring face pulls, open hand drag, shoulder Y's to I's and sloper rollers. The cycle sets the sets and weights each week.
plan.spacing: Light day: best the day after a heavy session

plan.what: A normal climbing session, for days you are too tired for the board. Counts as a training day, but does not tick off Finger, Board, Pull or Weakness.
plan.spacing: Any day; does not use up the Finger and Board gap

plan.what: Three 10–15 minute slots a week, on rest days or after sessions. Seven stretches: hip raises, pigeon, weighted pancake, wrists, toe touch, low lunge and side squats.
plan.spacing: Any day; not counted as a session

rules.title: Spacing
rules.text: Finger and Board go at least 48 hours apart, because they load the same tissues.

rules.title: Light day
rules.text: Weakness is your light day. Do it the day after something heavy.

rules.title: Pull day
rules.text: Done on the same day as Finger, since it is easy on the fingers. They are logged separately, so doing one does not tick the other.

rules.title: What to do next
rules.text: Do whichever session is most overdue that the rules allow. If you are tired or your fingers are sore, drop to Weakness or stretching.

rules.title: Full week
rules.text: Three training days: Finger with Pull, Board, and Weakness. The other days are free for climbing.

rules.title: Short week
rules.text: Finger with Pull, and Board, come first. Weakness goes last.

rules.title: Cycle
rules.text: Seven weeks plus a benchmark week: four build weeks, a deload, two intensify weeks, then retests. Finger loads are a percentage of your latest Tindeq peak, so a new test changes next week's numbers. The deload halves the sets in Pull and Weakness.

rules.title: Weaker hand
rules.text: Left hand goes first in every set.

rules.title: Rotator cuff
rules.text: Once a week, with Pull (rotator cuff rows).

rules.title: Shoulders
rules.text: Trained on Pull day and tracked there, not as a separate weakness block.

rules.title: Boards
rules.text: Tension climbs are tracked as Tension 1 to 3 and MoonBoard as its benchmark list, both boards at 40°. Log the number of tries on each climb you send.

rules.title: Readiness
rules.text: Log a 1 to 5 on each session. 1 or 2 means a light day.

rules.title: Assumption
rules.text: Strength figures are Tindeq peak pull (force, not added weight). Holding a one-arm hang needs margin over a one-off peak.

rules.title: Tired day
rules.text: Log a normal climb instead of a board session. It counts as a training day, and Board stays open for the week.

rules.title: Single exercises
rules.text: Open Pull or Weakness and tick off the easy exercises one by one. They count for the week (last 7 days). Tick off every exercise and the whole session counts as done.

rules.title: Shoulder work
rules.text: Rotator cuff rows and I Y T (Pull day) plus face pulls and Y's to I's (Weakness day) add up to about 18 sets of cuff and rear-delt work. Keep them on different days. The app warns you if you tick or log both on the same day.

Weakness.title: Weakness session
Weakness.intro: A gym strengthening session for the weak spots climbing does not fix by itself: pinch, heel hooks, shoulders and open-hand grip. Do the exercises in this order and tick each set as you finish it.

exercises.name: Pinch block lifts
exercises.how: One hand at a time, with the weight you have set.

exercises.name: Heel hook floor raises
exercises.how: Finish one side, rest 30 seconds, then do the other side.

exercises.name: Open hand drag
exercises.how: One 10 second hang at a time.

exercises.name: Shoulder Y's to I's
exercises.how: Lie face down with your arms lifted off the floor. Start with your arms straight, then bring them to your sides with the elbows bent at a right angle.

exercises.name: Sloper rollers
exercises.how: Weighted roller on a rope. Spin it both ways so you train open grip and closed grip.

Pull.title: Pull session
Pull.intro: Do one main pull, then the two shoulder exercises. Finger training happens on the same day but is logged separately, so logging this does not tick Finger.

variants.name: One-arm slow declines
variants.how: One arm at a time, lowering slowly.

variants.name: Lock offs
variants.how: Each rep: hang for 7 to 10 seconds at 90 degrees, then at full lock, on each arm.

exercises.name: Rotator cuff rows
exercises.how: Sit down with your arm resting on your knee and rotate a weight over the knee.

Stretching.title: Stretching routine
Stretching.intro: Tap Edit on any stretch to change its sets, reps, hold time or description.

exercises.name: Wide leg hip raises over bottle
exercises.how: Sit on the floor with your legs wide apart and your back straight. Put a bottle on the floor beside one foot. Keeping that knee straight, lift the leg off the floor, over the bottle and back down. Do both sides.

exercises.name: Pigeon pose
exercises.how: From all fours, bring one knee forward and lay that shin across the floor, with the other leg stretched out behind you. Lower your hips and, if you can, fold forward over the front leg. Breathe slowly and hold, then swap sides.

exercises.name: Standing weighted pancake
exercises.how: Stand with your feet at least double hip width apart, toes forward and knees straight. Hold a weight and hinge forward at the hips with a flat back, letting the weight pull you deeper. Hold, then stand back up.

exercises.name: Wrist stretching
exercises.how: Straighten one arm in front of you. With your other hand, gently bend that wrist so your fingers point down and hold, then bend it so your fingers point up and hold. Keep the elbow straight and stop short of pain. Do both arms.

exercises.name: Standing straight leg stretch
exercises.how: Stand with your feet about hip width apart and your knees straight. Hinge forward at the hips and reach toward your toes, keeping your back long. Hold where you feel a strong stretch behind your legs, then roll back up slowly.

exercises.name: Low lunge hip stretch
exercises.how: Step one foot forward into a lunge and lower the back knee to the floor. Squeeze the back glute and tuck your pelvis, then shift your hips slightly forward until the front of the back hip stretches. Do not arch your lower back. Do both sides.

exercises.name: Wide leg side squats
exercises.how: Stand with your feet wide and toes turned out a little. Shift onto one leg and sit down into a deep squat on that side, keeping the other leg straight with the heel down and toes up. Push back up and shift to the other side. Hold a weight at your chest for extra load.

planNote: Finger and Pull share one day, so training takes three days a week and the rest are free for climbing. The Cycle tab sets this week's numbers.

clashes.title: Lots of shoulder work for one day
clashes.advice: It is better spread over two days so your shoulders can recover. If you do both anyway, halve the sets of each and stop a couple of reps short of failure.

cycle.name: Cycle 1
cycle.intro: Seven weeks, then a benchmark week. Weeks 1 to 4 build, week 5 is a deload, weeks 6 and 7 push hardest, and week 8 repeats the tests from the start. The finger work leads; pull, pinch and sloper work is set to keep improving without competing with it.

phases.Build: Steady progression. Controlled hangs, clean reps, and weights that go up only when the last session was clean.
phases.Deload: About half the sets, lighter weights and no hard tries. Fingers and shoulders catch up, so the next block is stronger.
phases.Intensify: Fewer, heavier efforts after the deload. Shorter sessions, longer rests, and one-arm attempts in week 7.
phases.Benchmarks: Rested retests of everything that was measured at the start. Then the plan changes.

weeks.title: Baseline and settle in
weeks.aim: Get the starting numbers down and learn the loads. Everything should feel controlled.

finger.note: Left hand first in every hang. Note how many hangs feel solid, not the last one that scraped through.

sessions.Board: Pick 2 or 3 Tension 7b+ candidates for the benchmark and give each a go. On Tension 1, work the 7a and 7a+ climbs. Log the tries.
sessions.Pull: Weighted pullups, then rotator cuff rows and I Y T. Record a one-arm lock-off hold on each side as a baseline.
sessions.Weakness: Retest the one-hand pinch block max in the Tindeq app (the last one is from Jun 2025). Pinch lifts: pick a weight you can lift for 5 clean reps each hand.

p-pullups.note: Same as your last session. Only add weight once every rep of every set lands.

w-sloper.note: Same as now. Spin both ways.

w-pinch.note: Find your 5-rep weight this week. Write it down; it is the number to beat.

weeks.title: Add a hang
weeks.aim: Same weight on the fingers, one more hang. The pull-ups go up by a plate step if last week was clean.

finger.note: Left hand first in every hang.

sessions.Board: Tension 1: the 7a+ climbs. Keep one try on a 7b+ candidate at the end if your skin is good.
sessions.Pull: Weighted pullups: +2.5 kg if every rep landed last week. Then rotator cuff rows and I Y T.
sessions.Weakness: Pinch lifts: +1 kg if all 5 reps landed on both hands. Sloper rollers as set.

p-pullups.note: Add 2.5 kg only if last week was clean. Otherwise stay at the same weight.

w-pinch.note: Add 1 kg if all 5 landed on both hands.

weeks.title: Heavier fingers
weeks.aim: Fingers go up to about 90% of your peak. Pull-ups get heavier for fewer reps.

finger.note: Left hand first in every hang. Stop the set early if a hang feels like a grind; a clean 5 beats a ragged 6.

sessions.Board: Tension 1: finish off the 7a+ climbs and look at the 7b ones. Log the tries.
sessions.Pull: Weighted pullups, 4 sets of 4. Then rotator cuff rows and I Y T.
sessions.Weakness: Pinch lifts and sloper rollers go up a notch. This week's weights are on each exercise.

p-pullups.note: 4 reps now. Same rule: add weight only if the last session was clean.

w-sloper.note: Up 2.5 kg from the first two weeks.

weeks.title: Peak of the first block
weeks.aim: The hardest finger week before the deload. Finish it fresh enough to enjoy the rest week.

finger.note: Left hand first in every hang. This is the last heavy week before the deload, so leave one rep in the tank.

sessions.Board: Tension 1: aim for the 7b climbs. Cap yourself at 8 hard tries; skin and fingers are the limit.
sessions.Pull: Weighted pullups, 4 sets of 4, heavier again. Then rotator cuff rows and I Y T.
sessions.Weakness: Pinch lifts and sloper rollers at the same weights as last week, a bit more crisp.

p-pullups.note: The heaviest 4s of the cycle so far.

w-pinch.note: Same weight as last week unless it felt easy.

weeks.title: Deload
weeks.aim: Back off to let the fingers and shoulders catch up. Sets are cut to about half and nothing goes near failure.

finger.note: Left hand first in every hang. Easy hangs. If you are sore or tired, skip the Finger session; resting is the point.

sessions.Board: Easy climbing only: Tension climbs well under your limit, no projecting, nothing that hurts the skin.
sessions.Pull: Weighted pullups, 2 light sets. Then rotator cuff rows and I Y T, half the sets.
sessions.Weakness: Half the sets of everything, at lighter weights than week 4.

p-pullups.note: Light. Back off the weight for the deload.

w-pinch.note: Keep the weight from week 4 or drop 1 kg; just 3 sets.

weeks.title: Fewer, heavier hangs
weeks.aim: Fresh from the deload, so the fingers are ready for heavier loads in fewer hangs.

finger.note: Left hand first in every hang. Four hangs with a longer rest. Stop the session if your hand shape changes or your form goes.

sessions.Board: Tension 1: 7b climbs and the 7b+ candidates. Keep tries limited and rested.
sessions.Pull: Weighted pullups, 4 sets of 3 and heavy. Then rotator cuff rows and I Y T.
sessions.Weakness: Pinch lifts and sloper rollers to new top weights.

p-pullups.note: Heavy 3s. Add weight only if every rep of last time landed.

w-sloper.note: The target weight. If it does not move, repeat last week's weight.

w-pinch.note: Add 1 kg if the last session was clean.

weeks.title: Peak and one-arm attempts
weeks.aim: The final push. Heaviest hangs and your first proper one-arm hang attempts, rested and warm.

finger.note: Left hand first in every hang. After the hangs, try a few one-arm hangs on the right with as little help as you can manage. Stop at the first rep that fails.

sessions.Board: Tension 1: finish the list if you can. Rest well before the benchmark week.
sessions.Pull: Weighted pullups, 4 sets of 3. Then rotator cuff rows and I Y T.
sessions.Weakness: Pinch lifts and sloper rollers: top weights, no extra sets.

p-pullups.note: The last heavy week. Skip the weight jump if the last session was not clean.

w-pinch.note: Same weight as last week unless it felt easy.

weeks.title: Benchmarks
weeks.aim: Rested and fresh, repeat the tests you took at the start and see what changed. Then the plan changes for the next cycle.

sessions.Board: Day 3: Tension 1 list and a 7b+ attempt, fresh and rested.
sessions.Pull: Day 2: weighted pullups (+35 kg for 3 reps) and a one-arm lock-off hold on each side.
sessions.Weakness: Pinch block max in the Tindeq app, and sloper rollers at the top weight.

tests: Day 1: Tindeq 20mm peak, left hand first, then one-arm hang attempts. Pinch block max.
Day 2: weighted pullups and one-arm lock-offs. Sloper rollers.
Day 3: Board, Tension 1 and a 7b+ attempt.

goals.name: One-arm hang on the 20mm
goals.why: The main goal. Tindeq peak pull on the 20mm half crimp is the measure; holding a one-arm hang needs margin over a one-off peak.
goals.stretch: Stretch: right-hand peak at bodyweight, about 71 kg.

goals.name: One-arm pull-up
goals.why: Strength for the pull: the heaviest weighted pull-up set of 3 or more reps, plus a one-arm lock-off hold on each side. The full one-arm pull-up is a longer goal than one cycle.

goals.name: Pinch strength
goals.why: One-hand pinch block max on the Tindeq. Retest in week 1 for a clean baseline; the target is 10% above it.

goals.name: Sloper strength
goals.why: Sloper roller weight, the heaviest you logged for a set. Sloper force goes with how well people climb sloper routes.

goals.name: Tension 1 list
goals.why: A list of pinchy, sloper-based climbs. Every send counts, however many tries it took.

goals.name: A 7b+ in your style on the Tension Board
goals.why: The benchmark climb. Choose 2 or 3 candidates in week 1, give them tries across the cycle and log the send.

benchmarks.name: One-arm hang, right hand, 20mm
benchmarks.how: As little help as you can manage. Log the longest hold in seconds; 0 if you could not lift off.

benchmarks.name: One-arm hang, left hand, 20mm
benchmarks.how: As little help as you can manage. Log the longest hold in seconds; 0 if you could not lift off.

benchmarks.name: One-arm lock-off, right arm
benchmarks.how: Pull to the top with both hands, then hold the one-arm lock-off. Log the longest hold in seconds.

benchmarks.name: One-arm lock-off, left arm
benchmarks.how: Pull to the top with both hands, then hold the one-arm lock-off. Log the longest hold in seconds.

benchmarks.name: 7b+ on the Tension Board
benchmarks.how: Log the climb you send. In week 1, put your 2 or 3 candidates in the note.
